vid_urls.description:
Watch as mission experts discuss the science objectives for NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

Named for the agency's first chief astronomer, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's crisp, sweeping surveys will help scientists investigate dark energy and dark matter, discover and characterize exoplanets, map billions of galaxies, study black holes, and explore objects from our own solar system to the edge of the observable universe. 

Roman is scheduled to lift off at 7:26 a.m. EDT (1126 UTC) on Sunday, Aug. 30. Watch live here on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9wq3VHsL_bE

vid_urls.title: U.S. Spacewalk 98
vid_urls.description:
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and ESA (European Space Agency) flight engineer Sophie Adenot will begin a spacewalk at 8:35 a.m. EDT (1235 UTC). The pair will finish installing a high-speed communications antenna on the International Space Station; Menon and Adenot began the work on Aug. 18, 2026.

Menon will serve as spacewalk crew member 1 and will wear a suit with red stripes. Adenot will serve as crew member 2 and will wear an unmarked suit.

Learn more about this spacewalk: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/2026/08/20/spacewalk-preps-continue-to-finish-antenna-installation-job-next-week/

Get the latest updates from the space station: https://nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

Credit: NASA

image.name: US EVA Astronaut outside the ISS

description: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot will install a Space-to-Ground antenna on the orbital complex. The antenna is a critical communication system NASA uses to transmit data and high‑speed communication between the Mission Control Center in Houston and the space station. The astronauts also will replace a retroreflector used for spacecraft docking on the Harmony module’s forward port.
